chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the dowry, meaning in al-mut'ah (temporary marriage)?' He said, 'Whatever they agree upon, up to whatever period of time they choose.' I said, 'What do you think if she becomes pregnant?' He said, 'The child is his. If he wishes to establish a new matter, he may do so, and there is no waiting period (iddah) for her from him, but from others it is five and forty nights. And if she stipulates inheritance, then they are upon their condition.'
And this report does not contradict what was narrated...
ai.seo_question: What are the rules regarding dowry and waiting period in Shia temporary marriage (mut'ah)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the contractual flexibility of temporary marriage (mut'ah), emphasizing that the dowry is determined by mutual consent up to the agreed duration. It further details the legal implications of pregnancy, noting that the child belongs to the father and the waiting period (iddah) is extended to forty-five days if not divorced, while also permitting explicit stipulation of inheritance rights between the parties.
